title: Spaghetti al Limone
subtitle: Lemon, butter, and parmesan pasta
excerpt: A southern Italian pasta of striking simplicity: spaghetti tossed with butter, lemon zest, lemon juice, parmesan, and pasta water until the sauce clings and coats. Bright, creamy, and made in the time it takes the pasta to cook.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta al limone is associated with the Amalfi Coast and the lemon-growing regions of Campania and Sicily, where lemons are large, fragrant, and in season for much of the year. The dish is found in different versions: some use cream, some use only butter and pasta water to emulsify, some add basil. The cream-free version relies on the starchy pasta water and cold butter to build a sauce that is rich without being heavy.

content.text: The technique here is the same as cacio e pepe: the sauce forms from the emulsion of starchy pasta water, butter, and parmesan. Keep the heat gentle and toss constantly once you add the cheese so it melts smoothly rather than clumping. The lemon zest is added off the heat to preserve its brightness; too much heat kills the top notes and leaves only the acid.
Cook the spaghetti in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta water before draining.
In a wide frying pan over low heat, melt 20 g of the butter. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the lemon juice and 100 ml of pasta water. Let it reduce for 1 minute.

Add the drained pasta. Toss over medium heat. Add the remaining cold butter piece by piece, tossing constantly. Add the parmesan and continue tossing, adding splashes of pasta water to keep the sauce fluid and glossy. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from the heat. Add the lemon zest and toss once more. Serve immediately with extra parmesan.
